text_fidelity_a:
94 Piece First Aid Kit Packed with First Aid and Survival Essential by Sirius Survival A good first aid kit is a good thing to keep in the car when traveling and I selected this kit to keep in one of the vehicles because all of us are road warriors these days. Of course, the hope is that it is never needed, but when one is needed it's an invaluable resource. This is an interesting kit, and it has some pluses and minuses.

This is a small kit that fits nicely under a seat, in a seat pocket, or in a center console. Finding a place for it in a car or truck should be no issue at all.

There's a lot going on in this kit. It has a lot of the typical first aid items - bandages, gauze, cotton swabs, anticeptic wipes, and even a foil emergency blanket. There's some really odd things in here too - a flint, a compass, a whistle and a multi-tool are the stand-outs. This is not a typical first-aid kit but is also a basic survival kit.

The multi-tool is the standout in the whole kit and is worth the cost of the whole kit. It seems to be made fairly well, it is heavier than some of the cheaper ones I have seen and used and it has the basic tools you'd expect - pliers, a knife, screwdriver, etc. It includes a set of bits as well.

The compass is relatively cheap but it does work.

The remainder of the components in this kit are farily nondescript. All will work in an emergency capacity.

As a first aid kit this isn't so bad. However, this thing tries to be a survival kit as well, and on that basis there's an important omission - there's no flashlight in this kit. Even a small $5 flashlight would make this kit more complete and capable.

This certainly isn't a bad kit, but it tries to be two different things and as a survival kit it comes up a little short. This will serve well for a traveling family and in a pinch it will make a decent emergency kit, but I would not rely on it as a sole source.
text_fidelity_b: 94 Piece First Aid Kit Packed with First Aid and Survival Essential by Sirius Survival

text_fidelity_a:
BalanceFrom High Density Premium Muscle Relaxation and Fitness Foam Roller I’m a big fan of SMR (self myofacial release) exercises and stretching. They are easy to do and only require a roller, such as this. I can’t address the specific about the exercises in this review (do a search for myofascial release to learn more about the techniques and how they accomplish trigger point release) but rather will address only the roller itself.

This is a good quality roller. It’s the standard 6 inch diameter and is basically (like most other rollers) indestructible. It is a little less dense than other high-density rollers I've used, which is not a bag thing. I prefer that the roller has a little bit of give to it, since the ones that are rock-hard can be uncomfortable. On the other hand, I know people who prefer the rock-hard ones, so it’s more of a personal preference than a “good” or “bad” feature.

The surface is has a slight texture to it, but feels good against the skin. I didn't encounter any rough spots in the foam.

Some rollers have nubs on them to help stimulate trigger release points. If you are new to rollers, I’d suggest getting a smooth one such as this to start. Nubs take a while to get used to, and some people (myself included) can never get used to them.

I have the full-size version and find that best for back and full-body exercises. The smaller version (which I did not use) is better for targeted routines for specific upper or lower body areas.

Unlike other foam rollers this had only a slight “chemical” smell to it when I removed it from the wrapper, and the smell dissipated quickly.

My only quibble is that the ends are not perfectly flat – there’s a small elevated area at each end (you can see that in the product photo) which is most likely an artifact of how these are manufactured. It has zero impact in how the product is used, but does make it a just a little bit tippy when you store it on-end. Again, minor point, and it does stand up on end without toppling over.

This is a good choice if you’re looking for a roller. (And, if you’re not familiar with SMR, do take a few minutes to run a search and read about it – it can really make a difference!).
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: BalanceFrom High Density Premium Muscle Relaxation and Fitness Foam Roller

SYLVANIA RX2 OSRAM LED Bicycle Taillight Oddly, there are no instructions on how to open this light to put the batteries inside. I'm not recommending an additional piece of paper, but why not mention it on the card in the package? Anyway, you're just supposed to pry it apart with a coin. As I don't carry coins and rarely have one ready available, I used a butter knife. But I don't like this style of opening, and it's becoming less useful in modern society.

On that note, opening it made a few minor chips in the housing and I expect that to happen again and again. It makes it feel a little cheap. But being a little cheap is almost excusable since low weight is a priority for anything you stick on a bicycle.

I also don't like AAA batteries, as you get low bang/buck. But at least they last for a while.

All that said, most people are probably buying a light for their bike because they have to, not because it is some great hobby to ride the streets at night. Therefore, an inexpensive item that fits the bill is in order. And in that case, this is a perfectly acceptable light.

text_fidelity_a: Sleepingo Double Sleeping Bags for Adults Backpacking, Camping, or Hiking - Queen Sleeping Bag - 2 Person Sleeping Bag, Waterproof Double Sleeping Bags for Adults or Teens - Truck, Tent, Sleeping Pad A well-made, cozy bag for two! It's quite light, and not difficult at all to get into the compression bag, which has sturdy, well-sewn straps. Although I bought the bag for my husband and myself in case of emergencies, I've discovered it's very roomy and cozy for a nap, too (and the cats love to come nap on it with me—you can even use it as a comforter). The zippers seem to be well sewn and durable, and they work easily. It's convenient to be able to separate the two parts and make them into two single bags, if you want to. It IS helpful to have a light mat and ground cloth underneath, as with any sleeping bag, and I wouldn't say this is the bag you'd want for climbing Everest. Nevertheless, it's roomy and comfortable for two average-size people, and it even comes with two little pillows that are comfy without adding significant bulk. I'd say it's warm enough for three-season camping in most temperate zones, though you'd probably want to be wearing warm clothes or jammies, too, in a cool spring or late fall. All in all, for the price, I think this is a great hiker's bag!
text_fidelity_b: Sleepingo Double Sleeping Bags for Adults Backpacking, Camping, or Hiking - Queen Sleeping Bag - 2 Person Sleeping Bag, Waterproof Double Sleeping Bags for Adults or Teens - Truck, Tent, Sleeping Pad

text_fidelity_a:
Horizon Fitness T101 Treadmill I researched the hell out of treadmill before buying this one looking at costco, sams club, amazon, sears, etc and reading product reviews all over the internet. What sold me on this the most was the east of assembly and the sturdyness. My husband is 6'-2 and 300lbs. This has a 300lb deck and we have had no problems. Also what this offered over other models in the same class was 2" more of deck, a beafier motor and longer warrranty...all big pluses when you live in a rural area. A pleasant surprise on this model that wasnt listed was a cooling fan feature with three settings to at least move the air around your face when you get that heart pumping and a little sweat rolling down.
This is a fold up model, but I would like it more if folded up a full 90 degrees, but even at an angle, this has one of the highest angles that I've seen, folding at about at 65-70 degree angle...very much out of the way.
The thing is loaded with features, one which is nice is a VERY slow speed....1/2 mph...which for my extended family, is what my sneior father recovering from his second round of CHF needs. He know he needs to walk and has tried other friends treadmills, but they don't go slow enough...usually only .7 of .8 mph. The .5 mph in his exhaustive, delicate state is perfect to start and move him up to .7 and .8 mph for 5-6 minutes. Doesn't sound like much, but when your old and recovering, its alot. He's already seen an improvement in his endurance. On the other end of the spectrum, I like to move that incline all the way up to 10% and move out at 3 mph for 20 minutes (this is when the fan feels really nice, as does being able to plug in your ipod or mp3 player) and then back down to 2-3% grade for 10-15 minute cool down. Even my daughter is liking a treadmill.
I took us about 35-40 minutes to assemble...including unpacking from the box.
Delivery was great, though, because I am rural, I package actually arrived in Reno from the shipper within a few days, but then I had to way 3 weeks for the "truck" to have "a load" to head out into the rural areas for a delivery run. But when it did arrive, the driver moved it right into the garage for us (which sits 150 feet from the street). So 5 stars for the driver.
I can't really find anything that this treadmill doesn't do. I tend to buy things that fall somewhere in the middle when it comes to customer reviews, but a few things...like appliances, TVs and this treadmill, I wanted to get as much bang for my buck as I could. Yes, I would love to have the money to buy a Solei or other high end model, but for my family needs, my budget, the durability that it must stand up to, I am extremely pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Horizon Fitness T101 Treadmill

text_fidelity_a:
Elvira 32oz Large Water Bottle with Motivational Time Marker & Removable Strainer,Fast Flow BPA Free Non-Toxic for Fitness, Gym and Outdoor Sports For whatever reason, mine did not come with the strainer. If it did, I'd likely not have used it anyway, as I don't find a need to add fruit to my water. But since it was supposed to, I need to mention it. For some, it may be the very reason you select it. Product description states to contact them if there are any issues.

The bottle itself is solid. Holds a little over 32 ounces, has markings to help guide you in adequate water consumption, and the plastic is BPA free. I have other water bottle brand/style that I prefer-especially for carrying around with me, but this one has been good for use in the house through the day.

The bottle and lid is simple. The top screws on. There is a flip top with an opening approximately size of a quarter to drink from. If you want a larger opening, just unscrew the lid entirely. I prefer to do the latter to as it is easier for me to guzzle down some water that way. The wide open bottle is nice for cleaning purpose. And stuffing bottle with ice.

A good sized carry strap for convenience.

While the bottle cap feels secure, I am not inclined to toss this in a bag like my preferred water bottle. I am not too sure how well the flip top would stay on. I could be wrong, but I don't want to risk it. For me, this is strictly for around the house use. That being said..

I don't have too much trouble getting my water intake. I'm not on a diet, I have never noticed that drinking water helps with any of that, but I do prefer to stay hydrated and also simply enjoy plain cold water. Of all the bad choices I make for myself, I tend to always choose water to drink. I am a champ with getting my water in all summer, but I do slow up a bit come winter. I keep a 32 ounce bottle on me all day, and I even have another one at my bedside. This bottle is also 32 ounces (actually a little more, since the 32 ounce line is a few inches from top). The difference between my other bottles and this one, is that there is a little motivating factor through the use of time stamped on the bottle. The idea is to fill the bottle twice to get the recommended water intake. I thought if anything, this is what might remind me to keep drinking my water as we head into winter months. I wasn't sure if I was going to pay much attention to it enough to help me, but I find that the first thing I do in the morning is to fill my bottle to the top. I usually guzzle down 16 ounces almost immediately, After that, it is just a matter of looking at my bottle through the day, paying attention to the time, and making a point to take a good long drink. Refill and repeat. A simple, handy thing. My preferred bottles don't have that :)

And so, I am sold on the effectiveness of the time stamp. A little thing, but it does help. I don't need motivational quotes, just the easy at a glance view of my water level and the time. Good for me!

So I see no reason not to be happy with this bottle- unless you don't get the filter like me. . It is reasonably priced, good sized capacity that is easy to work with (basically drain and fill twice!). Cap off makes it easy to drink down a bunch of water, or just flip the cap to take swigs as needed. If you find yourself not drinking enough at once, I recommend drinking from wider opening.

Bottle is wide, may or may not fit in your vehicle cup holder, and as for carrying around casually in a bag.. still not sure how secure it is. It isn't subpar, just be mindful. Even with that consideration I recommend it, and consider it a 4.5-5 star product (if stays under $15)

EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit Wow..!! You’re looking at a small sized all-inclusive survival kit that really packs a punch! For the sake of not being redundant and listing included items (see photo I used with the list!) This kit albeit tiny in stature, really holds those basic “urgent” items.. just like circus clowns fit in a toy car!! The overall footprint is perfectly small!! No bigger then, a standard 3x5 notecard- Which makes it a great option to easily tuck inside your gear bag, backpack, tackle box, car glovebox, prepper supplies, etc. Best part of all, when added to a bag- this is so light, you won’t even know it’s there! Mission accomplished.

Love the container- its reminiscent of an old fashion sardine can but, with a useable lid to keep it securely closed.. Fact- the container itself is a working piece to this kits overall function! Giving a lot of thought into keeping this minimal. Of course, being this small in size- you should expect this is just for emergent necessities. This couldn’t sustain a person more than a crisis and certainly wouldn’t suffice for multiple people needs. Items included come in increments of x1 (bandaids = x5) So, if traveling in a group for more then a day.. I’d suggest a larger kit or, at the very least supplement this one.. This has the ability to get you out of a tight spot and would say that’s it’s intended purpose!

Note: One thing I’d definitely recommend with this kit.. and can’t stress enough- is including a simple how too handbook or, guide sheet to take with Ha! Starting a fire with flint isn’t like flicking a switch! If emergent scenario.. it’s safe to assume, the situation is not ideal! So, if ever found in position to use.. it makes sense to have that helpful 411. It may be difference of life/death. (Wow.. I sounded like Dirty Harry just then- ha ha..!!)

If you are prepping for serious situations that could present in your circumstances.. One must also acquire a full first aid kit, food/water supply, Shelter- to subsidize an item like this. BUT, hopefully that is common sense if you’re truly thinking through being prepared!

A few simple adds to make this more complete: Safety pin, small bic lighter (bc, I saw in a post- fire is harder to start then, one might guess- oh, wait.. that was me!) I clipped onto this case a carabiner with a built-in flashlight!! Just those few little items can beef this up a bit. (would have loved to see them included with the set.)

Overall, this is made to avoid being caught empty-handed and could definitely step up to that task 100%. At this price point- this is a great gift for those who love to venture out into situations where they may find themselves needing to be prepared- this will do just that!! I hope this info can help in your decision.. feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit

text_fidelity_a:
YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments My wife and I prefer weights as a workout, but both of us find the handles our community provides for the lat pull to be uncomfortable. The community provides the bar and nylon strap options, but 1. even with leather gloves they are uncomfortable, and 2. as a shorter guy my arm span is not such that I can get and maintain a comfortable reach (I can't hold the rubber grips on the bar), so for safety and comfort, I'm outta luck. But when I saw this YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for the gym I thought it might help me with comfort and safety, and be something she and I could both use to help improve.

The YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment is as easy as any attachment for the lat pull to get on and off, fitting the community's machine easily. There is a concern we have, but only time will tell if it plays out: the connection has a plastic exterior over what appears to be a metal disk, but we cannot tell how far that metal extends. It SEEMS as though it is only a disk and that the majority of the top piece is plastic. So we are not sure for how long or how much weight this connector will last. It is not that we have "proof" of it being subpar, just concerning by appearance.

The material of the rope itself also seems, not as overall strong, but as we are not at all experts in these materials or what is common in most of the heavy work gyms, we have nothing to compare it to. So we are going with it being an appropriate set up and provided materials. For our level of weights, even as I get stronger, we don't see it being at all an issue.

Lastly is the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment's handgrip, where you get that ergonomic element. I attempt to show in the various images how it is structured, curveted for the hand to rest within, allowing for a strong and comfortable grip. Again, I'm a shorter guy, so I also have a smaller hand. My wife's fingers are slightly longer than mine. We each find that the grip is both good and bad. We can each grip it and feel we have a secure hold. We feel safe. We feel a great pull. However, we each have a spot on the grip where it cuts into our finger/hand and begins to rub. In two images I show 1. the grip itself as I hold it up, then 2. my thumb over the top - it is at this point for me where it rubs and begins to feel like it's cutting into the thumb. Again, it is my hand size. My wife's issue is in the palm. She can fully and comfortably grip the handle, but at the base of the palm there is a cutting pressure.

So, do we like the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment? Yes, very much.
In spite of the issue and admittedly, with only using it twice for our full reps, we do like it. I will add, we have not worn our gloves during these workouts. We normally do, but circumstances had us in there without them, so using our bare hands, we did come up with discomfort whereby we got through the workouts, but didn't go full out as the discomfort grew. BUT, we both feel like once we have on the leather gloves the issue will at the least decrease greatly enough so as to allow us a full on workout and be okay. I will update if that does not pan out. But for each of us, the better grip and the overall feel of the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment as far as what we can do, how safe we feel, and even comfort to the greater part of our hands is enough. We went with the 4 star because of the issue, but WE THINK THAT if they were to add a more comfortable cushion (rubber, something) to the grip, this would be a great 5 star grip.
text_fidelity_b: YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments

Overall I'm happy with it for the price, but have to give it 4 stars due to some small issues mentioned below.

Pros:
Cheap
Seems durable
Takes almost no room when folded up
Easy to assemble and disassemble
Looks pretty nice

Cons:
Pretty wobbly - because it's basically thin aluminum, despite reinforcements on the legs the table moves around quite a bit. If you pin it against the wall and make sure the legs are really spread out it's workable, but still wobbly.
Sharp edges - there are some sharp edges that can really cut/bite you as your folding and unfolding the table. About 30 seconds with a file could fix this problem so it's a bummer they didn't bother.
Uneven top - the top has a crease where the table folds in half. This makes the top uneven, so if you have a laptop in the middle of it it kind of teeter-totters, which is a bit annoying.

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier This thing is totally awesome. I was actually unaware that such fishing rod carriers existed. And of course, I barely had to browse other models to tell Thule would be a top contender.

Construction is fantastic. Rigid metal tubes and hardened plastic casing make "vault" an acceptable term for this.

One thing I didn't realize was that with this one (unlike the tackle fishing carriers), the length is not adjustable. The tubing is the same diameter for the entire length, so the two 5' sections connect in the middle with a compression connector tightened by hex screws. Because of this, you probably need to lock both parts of this to your rooftop rack, which leads to me locking...

...Locking this up is probably the weak point for me. This is unfortunate, because I always want better locking on any device, but this one isn't even as good as I might expect out of Thule. For one thing, it doesn't have the "one key" feature that Thule started using at some point (but you had to special order your device with your key type already if you wanted to go with that, so maybe consumers were too lazy to do it and the company gave up on it...not sure). Worse, though - and a real concern - is that this and my tackle vault use the same key, which leads me to wonder if I am able to open up and steal from any Thule rodvault I see out there in the wild? (Of course, I'd like to believe that anyone with enough money to buy a rodvault would be unlikely to steal fishing stuff from another person, but who knows...). Also, you need padlocks to lock the vault to the rack, which isn't that big of a deal, but I've seen other equipment with integrated locks that used the same key as the rest of the equipment, so it could be better.

This is big and heavy. More so than I expected. That adds some sense of value to it, but it also has me rethinking my storage place, especially considering its 10' permanent length unless I want to disassemble it with every use.

I'm also curious if this would hold some deep sea poles. I think so, but don't have any yet to try for myself.

In conclusion, it's hard to not be impressed with this thing, and yet I see some areas for improvement, mostly in the locking scheme. It is hard not to give this a full five stars simply because of its excellent sturdiness and bringing a whole new excellent way to transport large, expensive poles with even a small car, and without having to worry about them at all, for the most part.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier

NCAA North Carolina Tar Heels Can Cooler, 16 I have this exact same cooler from another team, and got this one as a gift for my cousin, who is a huge fan. This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Tepui Camp Lounge Furniture Lawn chairs are useful for many purposes. They come in handy when you attend events and are a practical addition to your backyard. They are not all created equally, though, and one of the better ones I have used is this chair, the Tepui Single Chair.

Taken from its transporting bag, this lawn chair is ready to use- you just have to pull the legs apart and stand it up. This lawn chair is easy enough to fold back up and place into the carrying bag when you’re finished. I should point out that this chair is heavier than others so carrying it for a long distance could be tiring. However, it is also stronger and more durable than others. I am willing to put up with the added weight to have a better lawn chair.

I have several different lawn chairs for home and event use. This lawn chair from Tepui is an excellent one overall, delivering on comfort, quality, and strength. Nalgene OTF On-The-Fly Water Bottle - 24 fl. oz. (710 ml) I live an on-the-go kind of life. I'm always running from point A to point B with a big tote or a backpack full of things that cannot get water damage. I've used dozens of water bottles over the years and there's always been a problem: one is too big so it doesn't fit in my purse or water bottle pocket on my backpack, another leaks like nobody's business, another has a straw that just won't stay attached so you're sipping air most of the time, and others just don't lock up nice and tight.

One day, I was talking with my sister over lunch and I had noticed she pulled this water bottle from the dark recesses of her tote and nothing in her purse was wet. I was impressed. She had gotten this water bottle when she bought a 4 years ago and had used this water bottle exclusively since. She took it with her abroad and takes it to college classes everyday with no problems. After I hear her rave reviews, I decided to buy one.

I've been using this water bottle for a few months now and I honestly am in love. The slim design makes it unique compared to the typical Nalgene but it still feels very sturdy. Not quite a liter of water but it's more than the typically grocery story water bottle. The loop on the top makes it easy to grab on the go and even hook, via carabiner, to a strap or your bag. My favorite feature is the locking mouth piece.

In order to drink water, you have to flip the metal lock down and push the button to pop the lid off. I've read some reviews saying that this is too much effort but honestly, I love it. I know that the water bottle won't leak and it hasn't. I work in a school and I carry this around all day. Sometimes my students accidentally kick it across the floor and no water ever leaks. I also drop this bag into my gym bag and nothing gets damp ever. The small mouth piece also makes it great to grab a quick gulp of water while you're in the middle of a run. No twisting off lids: just flip the lock down, press the button and delicious H2O is delivered to your mouth with no spills.

Bottom line: buy this water bottle. I love it and I think you will too.

YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser for Home/Office Workout - Magnetic Mini Exercise Bike for Arm/Leg Exercise I've owned a bunch of under desk bikes, but I had specific needs when I bought the YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser - I wanted a heavier magnetic pedaler with the cranks as close to the front as possible so when pedaling with my arms, I wouldn't have to reach forward. Judging by the videos and pics, this was it.

The YOSUDA has a little rubbing noise - probably the belt - but it's still so quiet that it doesn't wake up my husband in the next room, and it doesn't affect the pedaling motion, which is super smooth. I've owned the MagneTrainer and the DeskCycle, and they're both silent and smooth, but for my arms the YOSUDA has a good crank rotation (8" compared to 10" with the MagneTrainer), and the pedals are much closer to the front than the DeskCycle. The DeskCycle and MagneTrainer are better built than this bike, but it's fine, and I love the handle. I've owned several $50 and under bikes, but there were universally louder and much less smooth than the YOSUDA.

I found the YOSUDA is also good for pedaling using your feet - it sticks to the floor pretty well when used at low resistance, and the pedaling is smooth. If you turn up the resistance, you may have to put it on a rubber mat to keep in in place, but at lower resistance, it stays where you put it.

My only issue about this is that the display is impossible to read in lower light. Since I use it in lower light, and don't care about the metrics, I just use the stop watch function on my phone to keep track of my time.

The YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser is pretty much what I expected from the description, the pics and the reviews. Mine has a little rubbing noise when I use it, which I wasn't expecting, but it's super quiet and otherwise IMO this is a very good pedaler for feet and arms. I got it for $125, and it's often on sale for that price or a little less, and for what I paid, I'm giving it back the star I removed for the soft rubbing noise and hard-to-see display, putting it back up to 5 stars. If it was $200 or more, I'd give it 4 stars, but it's a good bike with forward pedals, quiet and smooth operation at a reasonable price, so it gets 5 stars from me.
text_fidelity_b: YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser for Home/Office Workout - Magnetic Mini Exercise Bike for Arm/Leg Exercise

I just like to help people make a decision on purchasing affordable gear. Many times I have bought less expensive gear and was sorry I did. However this won’t be the case with Schrade. If you are just getting into camping/bushcraft start with this knife. I bought my knives directly from the Schrade website (shut down now) about 2-3 years ago. I have 3 of their knives Sch37, Sch57, and Schf52; and was only out of about $60 for all 3. They are great knives for a beginner. Yes, they have some issues. But they may not bother everyone.

The Bad: The basic handles are not the most comfortable over long periods of use. Later, get the micarta scales the basic scales are not comfortable when chopping or don’t chop.

The chimpping on top is a bit aggressive when not wearing gloves and doing percussive tasks.

The protective coating scratches and stains but; it can be removed and cleaned if you have the time. I like to keep my things looking brand new. I may remove the coating at some point.

The sheath is not the greatest but at least you don’t have to buy one.

The good: it comes with a sheath, a sharpening stone, and a fire steel. You don’t get that with $500 knives.

It can accomplish every task a $500 knife can.

You can sell the knife/knives for what you paid; if you want to upgrade.

You can keep them to loan out or for a buddy to use.

Best of all is the price. You get to test out your skills for less than $30 bucks with this knife.

text_fidelity_a:
Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

I bought this based on it conforming to the face and being Therapeutic. However, I often sleep with my head raised up or in my recliner because of breathing issues due to my sinuses.The silk of this pillow would always cause it to slip down or sideways causing me to wake up and recenter it on my eyes. Overall, I would recommend this pillow for someone who doesn't have to sleep with the head or upper body raised at any height and doesn't have to turn their head much while napping. The silk does have a cooling effect and the lavender and chamomile does help to relieve some of the pressure and pain.
text_fidelity_b: Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow

G4Free 2/4/13 PCS Camping Cookware Mess Kit Hiking Backpacking Picnic Cooking Bowl Non Stick Pot Knife Spoon Set This is a decent set of camping cookware consisting of four pots, each with handles (but no lids). The set nestles together into a pretty compact stack that measures about 7 inches tall and about 5 inches wide. It also comes with a mesh pouch to hold the pots when they are stacked together. It makes for a small, easily toted package.

The build quality is decent but not exceptional. The pans are aluminum and somwhat thin. The metal is thick enough so that the pots won't dent easily, but you can flex the pan if you squeeze them hard. The handles have a silicon coating on them which is nice for helping with heat protection (although you still need a mitt or pad to grab the handle if the pot has been on the fire for a while). The handles fold easily and take up very little room. However, the bracket that attaches the handles to the pot, as well as the handles themselves, are not all that sturdy. They are functional, but won't stand up to much (or any) abuse.

The pot sizes are fine for cooking for one or two people (perhaps you could stretch it to three if everyone is a light eater).

For occasional camping (or the rare emergency) use, these are more than durable enough to get the job done, and do so in a very space-conservative fashion. For that, I'd give them 4-stars. If, however, you're an especially avid camper, or need to cook for more than two people, you'll probably want a larger, more durable set.

text_fidelity_a: Neo Nautical Sundial Compass George Australia Sundial Watch Camping Hiking It’s a beautiful compass and the case is nice. I saw other reviews that said east and west were mixed up on their compasses. When you look at this compass, the painted end of the needle will point towards N on the rose when you’re facing N and it will point to S on the rose when facing S. However, the painted end of the needle will point towards W on the rose when you’re facing E and it will point to E in the rose when you’re facing W. As this isn’t an orienteering compass there’s nothing for you to adjust so that it shows the direction of travel. text_fidelity_a:
Carbon Tactics Quicky - Magnetic Tactical Belt (Regular) I quite liked the idea of the Carbon Tactics Quicky. A superstrong belt that could double as a strap, plus a cool buckle? Count me in.

First off, the buckle is very well-thought out and designed. I found myself playing with it, because it’s fun to open and close. All you have to do is press down and twist to open, while closing is even easier, thanks to the magnets. This could be helpful if you have trouble with regular belts. I haven’t ever had it accidentally open.

The nylon of the belt strap feels very heavy duty and secure; my mom actually used the belt for therapy, to help stretch her legs. She worried that lighter weight straps would break or slip free from her grasp, but she didn’t have that fear with the Quicky belt.

However, when I tried to use the Quicky *as* a belt, I ran into some problems. I wear a 30” waist in jeans, so at 50” long, the Quicky belt was very long for me. There’s an elastic loop to secure extra length, but if you pull in as much of the belt as I did, there was an unsightly/unsafe gap between my waist and the excess length. I *could* cut the belt strap to make it shorter and get rid of that unsafe gap, but then I would be limiting myself on other uses for the belt. While the inventor did a good job with other aspects of the belt, I wish he had considered other options for when the belt is used on a smaller waist.
text_fidelity_b: Carbon Tactics Quicky - Magnetic Tactical Belt (Regular)

text_fidelity_a: Hornady 46045 Neck Size Die 30 Cal .308 I purchased this neck sizer die specifically for my outdated RCBS neck sizer die with worn expander ball. Hornady's elliptical expander replicates those used by bench rest shooters as it sizes both on the insert and exit of the case from the die. If you have any irregular shaped case mouth,this expander spindle will straighter out the eccentricity while using. I find it a little time consuming if used for other .30 caliber change-overs such as .308 and 300 Win as you have to dismantle the setting in order to accommodate longer or shorter cases. I'm not a fan of Hornady's "Zip Spindle" system as it requires 3 tools to properly tighten the zip knob or the spindle will slip if the nut is not squeezed tight enough against the interrupted threaded nut. A second necessary wrench absolutely is Hornady's New Dimension red die wrench for this propriatory flatted die lock ring also available from Amazon. I lock the flatted die ring and die into my press,then finally tighten the small zip spindle nut using my Hornady wrench. The new dimension lock rings are great as the tightening screw impinges the 7/8-14 die threads at a tangent to the threads thus not marring the steel threads as most setscrews do. text_fidelity_a: Mountainsmith Day Lumbar Pack One of my favorite bags.  I bought this one for a family trip to Walt Disney World so I could be the family pack mule.  Although a backpack may look larger, I would argue this has as much internal cargo capacity as most backpacks out there.  I prefer this over a backpack because of its versatility.  I can wear it on my hips and twist it around as-needed.  Sometimes I'd wear it on my side for accessibility; most times on my butt behind me.  Sometimes I'd spin it around to the front to wear in my lap on rides.  Also, if you get tired of carrying it on your hips, I also used it as a cross-shoulder bag.  You can also carry it like a briefcase.  Once I really had the bag loaded heavy and it got tiring on my hips --- for those rare scenarios, you can also use the should strap as additional support while on your hips, too.  Many pockets, straps and hidden compartments.  I may just decommission my backpack that I use for the beach and use this.  I can see how this bag would be great for hikers, tourists, beachgoers, visiting amusement parks, etc.  It's worth noting that while there is a ton of storage, you can also cinch-up the straps and only put a little bit of stuff in there and the bag compacts a bit.  I bought a D-Clip for the molle loops to secure my hat/visor when not in use and I also used that looped yellow-cord on the front more than I thought for my sweat towel or to hang my kids' towel or hats.

text_fidelity_a:
MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag This tent seems like a great value at first. But when you can't sleep because of water seeping in, then drive yourself mad trying to tear down the tent in the morning you'll regret not buying a real tent.

The only plus I can give to this tent is that it sets up super easily. But to be honest, it's not really that much better than just setting up any other tent. The mechanism they have to pop the tent open works. But you're adding a lot of weight and mechanical complexity to something that's not very difficult in the first place.

On to the negatives.

It's impossibly annoying to tear down. While the tent pops open easily, it's a total pain to close. All of the plastic arms will start popping out of the mechanism. There's 8 joints you need to pull and close, one by one. And then you have to figure out which way the thing actually closes. But there's so much tension in the arms attached to the central hub that if you don't do it just right everything starts popping out.

So instead of just popping your tent poles out of the ground and pulling them out of the tent, you have to tear apart and rebuild this complicated lever mechanism spring loaded hub thing in the middle of the woods. And that's after you got no sleep because there's water in your tent.

The rain fly doesn't cover nearly enough of the tent. So if there's any rain it will rain directly on the tent, where as I said above, water will start seeping through into the tent. not just a little dampness. We had actual puddles in the tent.

I've had $20 Walmart tents that did a better job than this thing. It's not worth the money. It's overly complicated. And worst of all it just doesn't provide adequate shelter.
text_fidelity_b: MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch (WARNING- This is a long review. I am covering areas about this tent that were a concern to me. If you want a summary, go to the paragraph titled THE BOTTOM LINE)

I wanted to take the time to review this tent. I spent a LOT of hours researching, watching EVERY video and reading every available review I could find out there about this tent to decide which I would get. It was between this tent and [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]]. As it turned out, we had an immediate need for TWO tents, so I got both of them. You can see my review of the [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]] by clicking the link

WHAT IS THIS TENT LIKE?
One of the things I was concerned about was the thinness of material. We live in a very high elevation and get constant breezes or wind. There were a number of reviews that spoke of their tents snapping or ripping after only a gentle breeze. The fabric is thin, yes. But it does hold up.

Enough people have posted photos, so I won't post one as of yet. The best way to secure this tent is to ALWAYS leave the fly on. An unexpected storm or wind can come up at any time, and I personally feel that the tent is much more stable with the fly on than without. Make sure that you always stake down everything, including ALL of the ropes. That is what keeps the tent stable and secure.

FLOOR
The floor is very nice, and if you use a tarp underneath and take off shoes before entering, it will last quite a while. I also recommend not using chairs with small pointed feet on it either- it will wear out the floor quickly.

WINDOWS
The windows are perfect. They are protected from all but the most severe of rainstorms so you can leave them open if you like. The back window is open at all times, yes, but if staked down, it is not that big of a deal. If we plan to take this on crowded camp sites, I will sew two rings at either back seam and attach a thin fabric when changing. No big deal.

POCKETS AND LANTERN RING
The pockets are nice and in a good space. There is also a ring for hanging a lantern on if you like.

HEIGHT
The height is perfect for us- the tallest is 5 ft 9 inches. Taller people might not like this tent. The screened in porch is a bit narrow for those with long legs. You pretty much need a chair to use it unless you are a kid and don't need to lean back.

SCREENED IN PORCH
I LOVE this thing. I really do. This is my happy place. It is perfect for two camp chairs to look out at night or in the day. The door of the tent can stay open adding to a spacious feel. It does get wet in the rain. I am currently designing a fly to go over the porch and roll up into the tent when not in use. So far I am almost done with the one half of the fly and plan to finish the other half this week if I can. I hope to do that before the tent is taken down.

Without a fly, your stuff will get wet. There is an area that you can sweep the water into when wet, I use a sponge mop to clean it up so it will dry faster. Otherwise it puddles and does take a long time to dry.

POLES
The poles went up well for us, but you just have to take your time when putting up the tent. Do not race through the process, the fabric can rip if you don't.

TENT SPACE
Our biggest concern was ACTUAL usable space for us. We found that putting a queen inflatable double height mattress in there (Coleman) we have plenty of room for two of us. If using an additional single mattress, we can still do it, but it works best with a sleeping bag on the floor and picked up at night if a third person is in there (child).

When using or covering up the porch in rain, the porch makes a great extension for activities, talking, or just sitting and enjoying the view (if not raining). I absolutely love the design of this tent.

LIGHTING
The tent color is half of the beauty of this tent. The light bright colors are cheerful, let in a lot of light, and also keep it from feeling gloomy on rainy days. At night you can see through it, so keep that in mind when you are getting ready at night.

DOES THIS STAY UP IN STORMS?
The big question. I have an answer for you. We purchased this tent the week before Labor Day (US). We put the tent up immediately and treated it with silicone spray. We didn't need to- it is already made from silicone impregnated ripstop nylon. The seams also came pre-treated with silicone on the fly. AMAZING!.

We have had this tent up with daily use since then and it is now October 8,2016. So far it has been through extreme heat, breezes, high winds, thunder storms, all night rains, and heavy rain storms. The tent has stayed up with no observable damage at this point and stayed very dry too.

IMPORTANT POINTS
After reading MANY reviews on this tent, I decided to help it stay up, I would reinforce different areas. Anywhere that there is a plastic hook, I put a piece of garden twist tie into the fabric loop that holds the hook and tied it around the pole to help it absorb any shock of high winds. Any other plastic rings or hooks were reinforced in the same way. I tucked the ends of the twist tie way under so no chance of the fabric blowing into sharp edges and tearing in high winds.

STAKES
I also recommend getting other stakes for the tent. They stay in the ground during storms more easily too. I got [[ASIN:B01IEBKK92 Pack of 16, 7075 Aluminum Outdoors Tent Stakes & Rubber Hammer & Guyline Tensioner with Reflective Pull Cords & Carrying Pouch]] to use in the fly staking process, and used the ones that came with the tent for the actual tent staked to the ground.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Honestly, this is my favorite tent of all time. It is my happy place. I absolutely LOVE the design, set up, colors, and ventilation of this tent. With a mattress, it is still private to lay down with the windows open and you can still look out at the sky and enjoy the scenery. When you are in the tent and want to have breeze, the front door open makes it seem so airy and wonderful. I can not rave about this tent enough. Five weeks of constant use is more than we planned for, but it has held up so far.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED at five stars.

QUESTIONS AND UPDATES
If you have any questions I have not answered, by all means ask. I hope I can be helpful, as I know how it helps me when others do the same. I will update with any more input should I have anything else to share or if there are problems with the tent.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch

Osprey Packs Pandion Daypack The Osprey Pandion Daypack (OPD) is the best backpack I've ever had. No detail has been overlooked. It has everything. I'm still discovering features I didn't notice over the first few days.

I use my backpack for four things - schlepping my documents and portable office supplies for work back and forth to the office, for carrying my portable electronic supplies, for clothes/toiletries etc. for short airplane trips, and for long day hikes. I did all of this and more last weekend when I traveled to New Hampshire for three days which included a four mile hike, and two days when I needed to check in at work using my laptop.

There are three main compartments, each of which has its own partitions, sleeves, a lanyard, and in one of them, a waterproof lining. The pack itself has a stiff outer frame that comes in hand for a long hike, makes it easier to stand the pack up on its own, and allows for pack to be flattened out for light cargo, or fully expanded for air travel or a large payload. There are multiple exterior sleeves for water bottles, papers, and other items that are convenient to have quick at hand. Each zipper features a plastic loop which makes them easier to grab and pull.

The pack has multiple pull tight straps in a variety of places, including waist and chest straps that makes it easier to carry heavier weight, or using the straps on the outside, compress it down for lighter trips back and forth to the office. Its got a stout handle at the top. Taught mesh fabric has been stretched between the frame in the back, which provides good comfort for toting heavier weight, and allowing air to get in behind your back as you are moving along.

It's good looking, light, and it comes with a lifetime guarantee. Please peruse the multiple photos I took of the pack a few days ago (as usual, having difficulty with Amazon photo upload functionality. I'll add photos after balance of review posts.) This is a very impressive daypack from all standpoints including function, appearance, features, and weight.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Packs Pandion Daypack

text_fidelity_a:
Energizer Vision HD Performance Metal Flashight Lots of confusion on the reviews concerning this product mostly because two very different models were submitted to reviewers. This review is for the smaller 250 lumen model that takes three AAA batteries. It is short (about 3.75"), sturdy, and comes with three AAA batteries and a lanyard. The case is attractive with an industrial look but probably too smooth as far as texture for some people to work with. And yes, the package was relatively difficult to open, probably to discourage five-fingered shoppers from stealing them off the shelves. Unfortunately there are no instructions included for those who may not intuitively figure out how to install the batteries and use the three lighting functions (high, low, strobe).

Being short, slippery, and not confidence inspiring as far as using it -- and only having an estimated 2.5 hour battery life -- what is this really good for? The functionality is in its small size and very bright light. This would be an excellent tool for those working in small and dark spaces, casting enough clear and bright light for close detail work. Working under a sink with a Maglite LED 3D Cell Flashlight just doesn't cut it. This Energizer is small enough to prop up against anything in your work area to help focus the beam while freeing both hands for whatever task you're undertaking. The light beam cast by it broadens quickly and the choice of a "high" and "low" setting increase its usefulness. Believe it or not, it can actually be too bright for close work using the "high" beam.

This 250 Lumen Energizer is fine for short operating periods either inside or outside the house. However its very limited battery life restricts it to use as a back-up flashlight. For overall effectiveness as an emergency light source (blackouts, storms, indoor/outdoor security) nothing really beats a Maglite LED Flashlight using 3 D batteries. For $22.72 (compared to $14.99 for this Energizer) you have a 168 lumen light which casts a beam as far as 412 meters and has an eight hour battery life. We have several in our home that are red in color which makes them easier to find in a stressful situation. Not only that, but the Maglites are hefty enough to use as a striking weapon if need be. It's certainly better to have in your hand than nothing at all.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer Vision HD Performance Metal Flashight

text_fidelity_a:
MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set I have owned this 2-DVD set for several weeks now, and I am still on the fence about it. I researched it thoroughly before I purchased it, and the overall reviews seemed very positive. I am a daily exerciser and also a yoga instructor, but as I get older (I'm 49 now), I definitely have increasing aches and pains, and I know there are times when my lack of flexibility limits my yoga practice. I was hoping that Mark Lauren's Mobility Rx set would benefit me in these areas.

I will first provide a brief overview of the workouts, then detail what I liked/didn't like. Both DVDs have a Main Menu which includes selection for Introduction (Lauren's 2-minute explanation of these workouts, which you can find on YouTube), Warm Up (the same for both workouts, and Workout (1 or 2). There is also an option for Music on/off and Closed Captioning on/off.

The Warm-up is what Lauren calls a "movement prep," and it clocks in at 9:39 minutes. In has nice, full-body joint mobility work such as windshield wiper knees, hydrant hip rotations, trunk rotations, one leg bridges, lunges with torso twist, squat, and lunges with lateral reach. Workout #1 is 34 minutes total, including a 4 1/2 minute description of each of the four exercises. (Note that it is NOT easy to skip this. You can select the workout from the Main Menu without doing the Warm-up, but it is also NOT easy to return to the Main Menu AFTER doing the Warm-up for some reason.) There are three rounds in this workout, and they clock in at 8:53, 9:22, and 11:12. The exercises are side-lying snow angel, isometric lunge, zombie squat, and scorpion complex, and they get progressively more challenging with each round. Workout #2 has the same structure but with different exercises. This workout is shorter, with 3 1/2 minute introduction and three rounds of 7:24, 7:37, and 8:14 to clock at 27 minutes total. The exercises are seated roll, straddle reach, spider crawl, and gate swing complex. All of the exercises are well-described in other reviews for those wanting more details.

What I like about Mobility Rx is much shorter than what I don't like, so I will start with that.

WHAT I LIKED ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The exercises themselves. For the most part, these felt like functional fitness movements that definitely have the potential to benefit my body.
*The Warm-up. Although almost 10 minutes is long for a warm-up, this would make a nice little stand-alone stretch routine; it could also work as a cool-down after other activity.

Okay, that's about all I can think of, so on to what I didn't like.

WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The fact that they are on 2 separate DVDs. This may seem minor, but there's only a little over an hour of content, so making this set 2 separate DVDs not only feels wasteful to me but also feels like a marketing gimmick, as if they are trying to deceive customers.
*The very poor production values. Honestly, I often don't even notice these types of things on workout DVDs (and I have literally tried 100s), but there were MULTIPLE issues here, including the following: 1) the music - it was just bad, loud and on a repetitive loop (although at least there was a music off option), 2) the sound - it was out of sync with the screen, which is VERY annoying if you are actually looking at Lauren while doing the workout, 3) the menus - as mentioned above, options such as skipping forward and returning to the Main Menu did not work correctly, and 4) the set - also just awful, with a frame around the screen that appears as if you are looking into a 1980s computer and empty fake wood boxes stacked in the corner for no reason
*Lauren's instruction. Other than telling viewers to stand or sit with "tall PRETTY posture"--an awful expression that he uses over and over--he provides little instruction on form and absolutely no modifications. The initial preview of the exercises for each workout offers an anatomical view of the muscles being worked, but Lauren never refers back to this during the workouts themselves, never connecting the movements with the actual benefits for the body.
*The disparity between the two workouts. As you can see by my description above, the first workout is significant longer than the second, but it is also MUCH harder. The second exercise, the isometric lunge, is actually a lunge with the shin placed vertical against a wall/other structure. I would consider this an advanced movement--I have done it in yoga classes only after significantly more prep work than Lauren provides here. Similarly, the fourth exercise, scorpion complex, also incorporate yoga-type movements (plank and downward facing dog), and it requires a good deal of stamina and endurance.

In summary, I believe that these routines are appropriate ONLY FOR EXPERIENCED EXERCISERS. Although I definitely fall into that category myself, and I do see some utility to the movements Lauren offers here, the downsides of this set are a significant detraction for me, and I have not yet decided whether or not I will keep it.
text_fidelity_b: MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set

Color of the O-ring seems to vary. I have two black and one blue, but the Plano part number stamped into it is the same for all three.

CamelBak Flash Belt 17oz I wanted to like this belt because it is simple and lightweight, but it is expensive for what you get and I think there are a couple of important problems with the design. First, the main purpose of a hydration belt is to hold your water. This belt comes with an insulated water bottle, but the bottle is a non-standard size so you have to use their bottle. The bottle is narrower at the bottom than at the top, which helps you push it into its pocket. Unfortunately, no other bottles that I tried (including Camelbak bicycle water bottles) will fit (either the bottles are too wide or they fall out too easily).

Another problem is the single zippered pocket. The pocket will hold a phone up to about 6 inches tall. However, there is also a key ring in this pocket and I don't want my keys banging against my phone. I wish there was a smaller zippered pocket away from the phone pocket for keys. There is an open pocket on the other side that I assume if for holding energy gels.

The water bottle holds 17 ounces of water, which isn't that much, but that is usually plenty for me on a 1 hour run. Camelbak makes much larger hydration packs for hikers or mountain bikers that work well, but I am glad that have a lightweight option for joggers and runners. I just wish it was a little more functional and more competitively priced. There are lots of other runner hydration belts on the market.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Flash Belt 17oz

The bag has a large main pocket and a smaller front pocket. The backing is nice and stiff, but not rock hard. The mounting hardware and instructions are very easy to follow and uses mechanical anchors to avoid relying on simple friction to prevent bag movement. The optional shoulder strap is a good option for carrying the bag hands-free, but I feel sometimes as if I am carrying a purse. The quick release feature of this bag was a major factor for me. I carry quite a few small to medium work items with me in and out of buildings. The ability to detach and take the bag with me is a huge convenience.

Overall, after much research, I think I found a bag that fits my lifestyle well. It carries a nice amount of chachkes (yiddish idiom), is extrmemly portable, and installs easily. A good buy for the price.

Tasline Elite Pure Spectra Solid 8X Strand Braided High Power Premium Fishing Line Picture shown is 40lb on a Tranx 401HG

I have been buying from Australia and dealing with the shipping cost and time to get here, so very happy to see it here in Amazon.

This is an excellent braid. Over the years I have spent thousands and thousands of dollars on fishing braid trying to find that "one". If I don't like a braid after one or two sessions, I will pull it all off my reel and throw it in the garbage. I don't like lines that have dyes that bleed off. I also don't like lines that depend on coatings on them as they can have a waxy feel to them, which I feel affects the casting. Some coated lines also take time to break in, and some coatings eventually just wear off. This is one of the many things that makes Tasline so different. They don't use any dyes or coatings. So there is nothing to break in, wear off, or bleed.

Due to the diameter to breaking strain ratio of this braid, and I am able to get more line on my reel. I recently just spooled up 1000m of 20lb braid on my Tern 400. Tasline 20lb has a PE rating of 1.7 and breaks at 34lb which is absolutely perfect for slow pitch jigging setups.

Casting is phenomenal. I think that the 8 strand braids in general are just smoother than the more common 4 strand braids. This line is very quiet going through the guides, and knot retention is excellent.

*Each spool has a hand written number on the back which correlates with breaking strain testing data for that specific spool. My testing has shown that these numbers are accurate and true.

text_fidelity_a:
Seattle Seahawks Embroidered Nylon Flag We bought this flag to hang outside of our house on game day. I scoured Amazon for a couple of hours (at least) trying to find the best flag with the best value. I read a lot of reviews on a similar flag, in which most people said the flag was very thin. In my mind, thin does not equal quality, so I was highly drawn towards this flag because it's embroidered. Even though it was double the price, I figured the embroidery was worth it.

We received the flag in the mail pretty quickly, but immediately from its opening, the flag was bleeding color. :( Not sure if it was the thread they used in the embroidery, or the flag itself, but the white part of the Seahawks logo had significant purple coloring on it that looked like it was coming from the edges/embroidery. SUCH A BUMMER. We tried to see if we could wash it off, but it wouldn't come off, so naturally, we returned it. We live in Hawaiʻi where the weather is unpredictable and rains off and on a lot... so we didn't want more bleeding to occur while we hung it outside.

The flag was thick and felt like a durable and good quality material, but the bleeding was obviously a make or break for us. We ended up purchasing the "thin" flag that was half the price of this one and that one is perfect (despite being thin). Not sure if we just got a dud, or what, but based off of our experience, I wouldn't order this again.
text_fidelity_b: Seattle Seahawks Embroidered Nylon Flag
